image_description: A close-up portrait of a Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) head and neck. The duck has white plumage, a distinctive red caruncle (fleshy facial skin) around the eyes and bill base, a pale pinkish bill with an open mouth, and a dark eye. The background is blurred green/brown. A watermark 'Naturesbyte' is visible in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is pale pinkish/whitish, not dark grey to yellow-green. This is a Muscovy duck, which has a different bill color than the typical mallard drake described in the taxonomy.
The eye appears light-colored (greyish/blue) with a dark pupil, not uniformly dark as described for typical drakes.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body cannot be assessed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plumage is white with red facial caruncles, not matching the described mallard or chestnut-headed patterns. This is a Muscovy duck, not a mallard.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Legs and feet are not visible in this headshot.
Wings are not visible in this headshot.
